newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela gives Central Bank OK to issue T-bills.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela gives Central Bank OK to issue T-bills.

text.p: The Venezuelan government gave final approval Wednesday to a decree that will allow the Central Bank to start issuing Treasury bills alongside its regular Monetary Stabilization bills, or TEMs, Information Minister Fernando Egana said.

The long-awaited Treasury bills, "will strengthen the Central Bank's financial situation and grant it greater flexibility in the execution of monetary policy," Egana told reporters after a cabinet meeting of ministers.
The bills, which will be used to pay off the government's $3.6 billion debt with the Central Bank, add another weapon to the bank's currently limited portfolio of monetary tools.
Currently the bank is dependent on TEMs for its open market operations.
The government's debt with the bank stems from the Brady bond debt restructuring in the early 1990s.

Under original plans, the Central Bank was to issue 450 billion bolivars worth ($925 million) of Treasury bills this year. In subsequent years, bills worth up to 0.75 percent of GDP were to be issued.
The bills were due to carry maturities of six months to two years with a floating coupon adjusted quarterly.
Egana did not say whether these conditions had been altered.
